correctness.rationale: The normal map has rank three with the positive relation u₀+u₁+u₂+3t u₃=0. In a mixed sign orthant, rescale the signed absolute normal coordinates by the relation coefficients and normalize the sum on each sign block to 1. The resulting plane section is the product of the two simplices of dimensions p−1 and q−1, where p+q=4. This proves exactly two top-triple triangles of type A, six other triangles of type B and six quadrilaterals of type C. Spherical excess gives the stated areas. A local correction to RESULT.md line 51: in a quadrilateral the angle order is α,α,β,β up to cyclic order and reversal, not alternating. This follows from the square section: the two corners with the same active constraint on the sign block containing the fourth normal are adjacent. The angle multiset, excess, and every area and ratio claim are unchanged. The derivative ratio ρ=−α′/β′ increases from 0 to √3 and equals 1 at 1/3. Hence A−B switches sign there; C−B vanishes at both endpoints with derivative changing once from positive to negative; C−A starts positive, has one derivative turn, is still positive at 1/3, and tends to −2π. This gives the unique maximum-cell switch. On the first branch C′/A′ strictly decreases, and C/A exceeds its current value by the weighted-average formula and C(0)>0. Starting at 1/3, C/B is a tail average of the strictly increasing function 2(ρ−1)/(2−ρ), so strictly increases; A/B strictly increases on the final branch. The ratio diverges at both ends, and substituting t=1/3 and independently bisecting the switch give 2.465777523812557 and 0.519200060611418. The packaged checker was read, not executed.

value.rationale: This is a natural deformation of the classical tetrahedral net for an established great-circle objective. Its complete ratio law provides an exact benchmark with a non-obvious separation between the ratio optimizer and the change of largest-cell type, not just a recomputation of the tetrahedral areas. Its utility and scope are restricted to the specified symmetric family.
